rationale_overall: This week's pool shows a dense cluster of nuclear/SMR headlines (Trump energy-policy push, Meta signing power agreements with Vistra/Oklo/TerraPower, Wyoming reactor progress, uranium-producer optimism) plus a NuScale (SMR) analyst upgrade — but that's continued validation of the wave SMR already represents, not a signal that SMR itself has broken thesis or peaked, and TerraPower/Vistra are not clean like-for-like upgrades (TerraPower is private; Vistra is a diversified utility, not a pure SMR play; Oklo is intriguing but a single week's PPA headline isn't yet a 'clearly stronger' case to force a same-bucket swap out of SMR). RKLB continues to draw supportive coverage (Hegseth 'Arsenal of Freedom' visit to its Long Beach facility) with no fundamental breach, just a neutral 'is it still a buy after 174%' piece. NVDA and GOOGL saw only routine AI-stock chatter and competitive-landscape noise (AMD's CES chip, SK Telecom's own LLM), nothing thesis-breaking. Filtered out as noise: geopolitical missile-test stories (Iran, North Korea, Pakistan, India/DRDO) with no investable US ticker; private/non-investable robotics names (Boston Dynamics, Schaeffler, Samsung robotics, lab-automation webinars, school robotics competitions); the RKT (Rocket Companies, mortgage lender) vs RKLB (Rocket Lab) keyword collision; Mobileye's Mentee Robotics acquisition (interesting but not a clean pure-play robotics wave entry this week); vague 'quantum funding' headline naming no ticker; and generic listicle pieces ('3 best AI stocks,' 'safest trillion-dollar AI stock') that name no new catalyst. No genuine catalyst rose to the bar for a same-week swap; watchlist holds unchanged.
